verified.catalyst: Barrick plans a minority (about 10-15%) IPO of its North American gold business (NGM stake, Pueblo Viejo, Fourmile), targeted for year-end 2026, with Newmont's consent and settlement (a $1.95B payment to Barrick) already in hand and most net proceeds earmarked for shareholders.
verified.dated_milestone: Management repeated the year-end 2026 IPO target at Mining Forum Americas on 2026-09-29. Next dated checkpoint is the Q3 2026 results on 2026-11-09, which should bring an IPO timing update. The registration filing (F-1/S-1) is still unfiled as of 2026-10-12.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 yes: Newmont is the named counterparty, with JV consent and a $1.95B settlement. G2 partial: management has publicly committed to a year-end 2026 IPO, but nothing is filed and there is no pricing or size document. G3 fails: there is no specific figure the market has not already priced. A 10-15% float does not force a re-rating of the 85-90% Barrick keeps, and the $1.95B settlement is public (about 2.8% of the $68.8B market cap).
verified.edge: L. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base: not cleanly measurable without a February 2026 price, because the move is dominated by the gold price. The stock rallied about 20% around the August settlement and Q2 results (SA 2026-08-20 and 2026-09-08 articles), then gave back from the $54.69 high to $41.06. That leaves it near its 50/200-day averages, so the drawdown is gold beta, not event decay. Remaining capture: an estimated 0-10% from the event itself. The case rests on a mark-to-market of the North American assets lifting the parent's multiple. SA (2026-10-06) argues today's price already pays about full value for Nevada and that the discount sits in Africa and copper, which the listing leaves behind. Most of the upside is therefore really a gold-price bet, which is a macro bet.
verified.primary_source: MarketBeat, "Barrick Mining Targets Year-End IPO as Nevada Growth Plan Takes Shape" (2026-09-29). GlobeNewswire, Barrick Q3 results date release (2026-10-09). Seeking Alpha, "Barrick Mining: Nevada Is Priced Like It Is Already Listed" (2026-10-06). FMP quote for B (2026-10-12).
verified.analysis: The event is real and was re-confirmed for year-end 2026 (2026-09-29 company event), but it is not filed yet and the next hard date is the 2026-11-09 Q3 report. Numerator provenance: Barrick has no preferred stock or external manager ahead of the common, and most net proceeds go to shareholders. The equity waterfall is clean, but a 10-15% minority float mostly converts NAV the market already credits into cash, not new value. Score capped at 4 because remaining event-driven upside is thin and swamped by gold beta. Gap: the web-search budget was exhausted, so I could not pull the latest 10-Q/6-K, the exact February 2026 base price, or the IPO size and proceeds math. Verification used only FMP quote and FMP news.

verified.catalyst: Aquarian Holdings' $70/share cash buyout of Brighthouse Financial (agreement dated 2025-11-06) is still waiting on insurance-regulator approvals (DE/NY/MA). Closing slipped to December 2026 under regulatory scrutiny and open questions about Aquarian's financing.
verified.dated_milestone: Outside date 2026-12-06 (auto-extended; I did not verify whether a further extension option exists). The next observable markers are NYDFS/DE/MA Form A approvals or a financing update, and Q3 results in early November 2026.
verified.instrument: BHF common (cash-out at $70). The non-cumulative preferreds (BHFAP etc., ~12% yield) are an alternative lower-beta expression, but they face delisting after the merger.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 (named counterparty: Aquarian Holdings) + G2 (signed definitive agreement, $70 cash, outside date 2026-12-06) + G3 (gross spread of $21.47, about 44%, currently unpriced)
verified.edge: M. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base: about -5% to -20%. BHF is at $48.53, below its pre-announcement and rumor-era trading range and near its 52-week low of $44.51, so nothing has been harvested. Remaining capture: +44.2% gross to the contractual $70. Taking a standalone break floor of about $40 (below the 52-week low; Q2 earnings missed and the stock is down 13.6% since then), the market implies roughly 28% close odds. If the real odds are 50-55%, EV is about $55-56.5, or +14-16%. The edge depends entirely on whether the market is overstating the financing and NYDFS risk, and I could not verify that here.
verified.primary_source: FMP quote for BHF ($48.53, 52-week range $44.51-$66.80), 2026-10-12. Seeking Alpha, 'Brighthouse Financial PFDs: Update With Acquisition Still Pending', 2026-10-06 ($70 cash, completion delayed to Dec 2026, regulatory scrutiny, Aquarian financing questions). BHF 10-Q filed 2026-08-06 (Aquarian agreement tag dated 2025-11-06; 57.51M shares outstanding).
verified.analysis: The deal is real, contractual and unfired. The price is a cash deal price, so numerator provenance is exempt, and the preferred stack doesn't touch the common's $70 cash-out. Residual capture is essentially the full 44% spread because the stock trades below its pre-deal levels. But a spread that wide two months before the outside date is the market pricing roughly a 70% break. Seeking Alpha (2026-10-06) confirms the delay to December under regulatory scrutiny and doubts about Aquarian's financing. I could not verify the commitment papers, the reverse termination fee, NYDFS's stance or the extension mechanics: the web-search budget was exhausted, and the 10-Q fetch was truncated before the merger note. So I hold at WATCH/6 rather than ACTIVE until the financing and Form A status are confirmed. A confirmed equity/debt commitment or one state approval would justify upgrading to ACTIVE 7-8.

verified.catalyst: Topline from QUELL-CV, BioAge's Phase 2 dose-ranging trial of oral NLRP3 inhibitor BGE-102 (primary endpoint: % change in hsCRP, three doses vs placebo), guided for 2H-2026 and not yet reported.
verified.dated_milestone: QUELL-CV topline guided 2H-2026 (first dosed 2026-06-16; guidance repeated in the 2026-08-05 Q2 release), so the readout should land by 2026-12-31. Next: Q3 10-Q / business update around early-to-mid Nov 2026, which should restate cash and whether the guidance still holds. QUELL-DME topline is guided 2H-2027.
verified.bloom_gates: G2 (company-guided dated readout: QUELL-CV topline 2H-2026, three doses vs placebo, primary endpoint hsCRP) + G3 (currently unpriced figure: market cap about $239M vs about $381M cash and investments at 6/30/26, roughly $355-360M after Q3 burn, so EV is about -$70M to -$120M). G1 partial only: Novartis/Lilly collaborations exist but are not tied to this readout.
verified.edge: M. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base: about -69%. The trial was publicly knowable 2026-06-16 with the stock around $20-23. It was crushed on 2026-07-31 when Novo's NLRP3 Phase 3 CV trial disappointed, and now sits at $6.34 against a 52-week high of $25.96, so nothing is harvested. Remaining to favorable resolution: about +60-90% (roughly $10-12, a re-rate back toward and above cash), against about -30% on a miss (around $4.5, a deeper discount to cash). Cash per share is about $8.0-9.5 depending on share count (45M weighted vs 37.6M on FMP's market cap), so the stock trades at about 0.65-0.8x net cash and that floor is largely unpriced. Two things keep this from H. First, the readout is low-binary on its endpoint: Phase 1 already showed up to 86% median hsCRP reduction, so a hsCRP hit is likely. Second, Novo's outcome failure undercuts whether hsCRP lowering translates into CV benefit, so a "hit" may not re-rate the class.
verified.primary_source: BioAge Q2-2026 results PR (GlobeNewswire, 2026-08-05: QUELL-CV topline 2H-2026); QUELL-CV first-dosed PR (2026-06-16); QUELL-DME first-dosed PR (2026-09-08); FMP 10-Q balance sheet and cash flow, Q2-2026 (filed 2026-08-05); Benzinga 2026-07-31 (Novo NLRP3 Ph3 sell-off); FMP quote 2026-10-12
verified.analysis: The catalyst is real, dated (2H-2026) and forward: QUELL-CV has not read out, and the stock has de-rated about 70% on Novo's NLRP3 class read-through rather than run up into the event. BIOA has no debt and no preferred stock (balance sheet 6/30/26: total liabilities $22M, mostly leases and payables), so the waterfall is clean and net cash of about $355M+ exceeds the $239M market cap. The upside comes from the event re-rate plus the cash floor, not from an inherited analyst target. The gaps keep it at WATCH: no exact readout date yet; the endpoint is a biomarker the Phase 1 data already de-risked, and an outcome failure in the class weakens its value as evidence; a share-count discrepancy (45M weighted vs 37.6M implied) moves cash per share by about $1.5; and burn of about $20-24M a quarter plus the new QUELL-DME trial will keep eating into the cash. Web search was unavailable this run (turn budget exhausted), so there is no confirmation that 2H-2026 guidance was restated at the Sept 2026 Morgan Stanley and Citi conferences.

verified.instrument: BIPC common (NYSE, $37.36), or as a pair: BIPC vs BIP ($37.10). BIPC shares exchange 1:1 into BIP units, but the exact simplification exchange terms were not verified
verified.bloom_gates: G1 partial (named counterparty Brookfield Infrastructure Partners / Brookfield; the transaction is internal). G2 partial (a dated shareholder vote, but the deal terms were not verified). G3 FAIL (no specific unpriced figure: the only mechanical lever is the BIPC-over-BIP premium, and it is now about 0.7%)
verified.edge: L. The structural lever is the BIPC-over-BIP premium. It was +3.5% on 2026-07-20, before the announcement (BIPC 40.55 / BIP 39.18). It fell to +1.7% by 07-24 and is +0.7% today (37.36 / 37.10). Run-up: of the event-driven spread, about 80% (2.8pp of 3.5pp) is already harvested. The absolute price ran up only about +2.5% in the first week after the announcement and BIPC is now -7.9% versus the pre-announcement base, a move driven by rates, not the event. Remaining: about 0.7% of spread is left at most, and if the terms are a plain 1:1 merger it favors short BIPC / long BIP, so there is no long-side event upside. Any upside on BIPC common is a rate/infrastructure-multiple macro view, not the vote.

What is left is a sub-1% pair spread, and BIPC's -8% since July comes from long rates, which would make this a macro bet. GAP: the web search budget was used up, so I could not check the exchange ratio, the cash/tax election, the index-deletion angle (BIPC could be removed from S&P/TSX or other indexes, forcing selling) or the closing date in the circular.
